title: Border Constraint Resolver: customer access policy and variant fanout
creator: Aisha Morales
description: Implement a Border Constraint Resolver service and runtime hooks that evaluate customer-scoped policies (EU-only residency, allowlists/denylists, tier routing) and emit deterministic routing decisions plus ordered fallback model variants. The resolver must be pluggable into the request path for hosted/dedicated/private, support per-tenant overrides, and expose auditable decision traces for Console and billing/SLAs.
acceptance_criteria: Resolver evaluates account-level residency constraints and returns route decisions with region and tier (e.g., eu-west-1,dedicated) for >99% of requests within 2ms median decision latency in local dev cluster
Customer allowlist/denylist rules are enforced: requests from denied accounts are blocked or routed to compliant alternatives based on policy
Fallback model variant fanout is returned when preferred model is unavailable; fanout includes at least two downgrade-compatible models and a last-resort remote-hosted option
Decision traces include policy id, evaluated predicates, selected model variant list, and reason codes; traces are persisted to audit log with tenant id and request id
E2E tests simulate cross-region capacity loss and demonstrate automatic failover to allowed variants without breaching residency for accounts that require EU-only
Console shows per-tenant summary of active residency policy, recent block events, and fallback counts
design_decisions: Policy model: hierarchical evaluation where tenant policy overrides global defaults; precedence: explicit deny > explicit allow > default routing
Representation: policies expressed as JSON schema stored in config service (immutable versioning) with a stable policy_id referenced in requests
Evaluation runtime: implement as a lightweight gRPC microservice with in-memory policy cache and TTL refresh; provide sidecar option for Private deployments
Fallback strategy: return an ordered list of model variants (primary, secondary, tertiary) rather than a single alternate to allow caller deterministic retries
Observability: emit structured decision events to EventBus (topic: routing.decisions) and write compact audit entries to tenant-audit store for 90-day retention by default
implementation_notes: New service: border-constraint-resolver (Go) exposing Evaluate(requestMetadata) -> Decision proto
Config: add policy schema to config-service, provide migration tool to validate existing tenant metadata
SDK change: Redwood client will accept decision_trace header; internal router will consult resolver before routing to model-serving mesh
Performance: aim for sub-2ms median by optimizing cache keying on (tenant_id, model_id, request_region_hint); benchmark early on t2.medium dev nodes
Security: resolver will validate caller JWT and check RBAC for tenant-scoped policy edits
Migration: default to backward-compatible behavior (if no policy present, solver returns existing routing)
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (dev): unit + integration tests; local dev sandbox with sample tenant policies
Phase 1 (canary): enable resolver for internal tenants and 3 opt-in customers with EU-residency policies; monitor decision latency and blocked request count
Phase 2 (beta): expose tenant controls in Console for editors; allow per-account safelists; increase retention of routing decision logs to 180 days for compliance customers
Phase 3 (GA): default-on for new accounts; migration tool run for legacy accounts; provide docs & runbook for support
Rollback: revert router hook to pre-resolver behavior and invalidate policy cache; run emergency bypass route for escalations
dependencies: CONFIG-1142: policy schema landing in config-service
CONSOLE-803: tenant policy UI and audit viewer
RUNTIME-557: router hook integration and header propagation
AUDIT-91: tenant-audit store retention and write throughput upgrade
test_plan: Unit tests for policy parser and precedence rules
Integration test: simulated cross-region capacity loss with traffic replay, assert no data egress for EU-only tenants
Load test: 10k evals/s calling Evaluate() with mixed tenants; decision p99 < 15ms
Property tests for fallback ordering and compatibility filtering (ensures selected fallback supports required features like streaming or function-calling)
End-to-end acceptance with sample customers and staged canary traffic
